14 A submarine has circular windows of diameter 0.30 m. The windows can experience a maximum
external pressure of 660 kPa before they crack.
What is the minimum external force needed to crack the windows?
A
47 000 N
B
190 000 N
C
310 000 N
D
620 000 N

hints: Notice the window diameter is $0.30 \text{ m}$, so the radius needed for the circle area is $0.15 \text{ m}$.
Connect the $660 \text{ kPa}$ maximum pressure to force using pressure $p = F/A$, so $F = pA$.
Calculate $A = \pi r^2$ with $r = 0.15 \text{ m}$, then multiply by $660\,000 \text{ Pa}$ and compare to the $47\,000 \text{ N}$ scale.
walkthrough: Identify the givens: circular window with diameter $d = 0.30 \text{ m}$, so radius $r = d/2 = 0.15 \text{ m}$, and cracking pressure $p = 660 \text{ kPa} = 660\,000 \text{ Pa}$.
State the governing rule: pressure is force per unit area, $p = F/A$, so the force on the window is $F = pA$.
Calculate the window area: $A = \pi r^2 = \pi \times (0.15 \text{ m})^2 = \pi \times 0.0225 \text{ m}^2 \approx 0.0707 \text{ m}^2$.
Substitute to find the cracking force: $F = 660\,000 \text{ Pa} \times 0.0707 \text{ m}^2 \approx 46\,700 \text{ N}$.
Check units: $\text{Pa} \times \text{m}^2 = (\text{N m}^{-2}) \times \text{m}^2 = \text{N}$, and round to about $47\,000 \text{ N}$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Using $F = pA$ with $A = \pi(0.15)^2$ gives about $47\,000 \text{ N}$, the force at $660 \text{ kPa}$.

B.explanation: This uses the $0.30 \text{ m}$ diameter as the radius, giving an area four times too large and about $190\,000 \text{ N}$.

C.explanation: This is much larger than $p \times \pi r^2$ and does not follow from the correct circular area with $r = 0.15 \text{ m}$.

D.explanation: This is about twice the $310\,000 \text{ N}$ value and far above the $pA$ result of about $47\,000 \text{ N}$.
